chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q4 Argument Essay (6 points) — Set 1: Federalist No. 10 / factions
chunks.content: AP Government FRQ 4 is the Argument Essay, 6 points across four rows. Row A Claim/Thesis [1]: a defensible claim/thesis responding to the prompt with a line of reasoning. Row B Evidence [0–3]: 1–2 points for relevant evidence supporting the claim; the 3rd point requires using at least ONE of the required foundational documents listed in the prompt (and requires the Row A thesis). Row C Reasoning [1]: explains how/why the evidence supports the claim (requires Row A). Row D Responds to Alternate Perspectives [1]: describes an opposing/alternate perspective AND rebuts/refutes/concedes it (requires Row A). Set 1 prompt cites Federalist No. 10 (factions as a threat) as a required foundational document. Common failure: never using a required foundational document (caps Evidence at 2); presenting but not answering an alternate perspective (loses Row D); a thesis that only restates the prompt.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4A, 6/6
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 6/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence 3, Reasoning 1, Alternate 1). Defensible thesis; evidence including Federalist No. 10 used to support the claim (earning the 3rd evidence point); reasoning connecting the evidence to the thesis; and an alternate perspective that is rebutted. Full-credit model for the argument essay.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4B, 4/6
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 4/6 — typically Thesis 1, Evidence 2, Reasoning 1, Alternate 0: a defensible thesis with evidence and reasoning, but the alternate-perspective point is lost (an opposing view described without rebuttal) and/or the 3rd evidence point is missed for not using a foundational document. Illustrates the common 4-point argument essay: solid claim and support without a full response to the counterargument.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q4 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 4C, 1/6
chunks.content: Q4 (Set 1) scored 1/6 — earned only one point, typically the thesis (or a single evidence point), with no adequate evidence tied to the claim, no reasoning, and no answered alternate perspective. Because Reasoning and Alternate Perspectives require the Row A thesis and a supported argument, a thin essay collapses to 1. Illustrates a claim without development.
